material_findings.C584: On five new small families, three-arm and two-arm both matched full-two live quality; three-arm used 17.29% fewer candidate compilations than full-two, two-arm 34.82% fewer, and seeded never won a commit.
material_findings.C585: Width+1 gate skipped seeded BDD work on 6/8 new families and matched always-three quality with 16.86% fewer compilations, but both gate opens were false positives and plain two-arm was cheaper with equal quality.
material_findings.C586: Frozen learned gate matched always-three summed live quality 1012 on 16 disjoint n=14 test graphs with 8099 vs 10020 BDD candidate compilations (19.17% fewer), and caught the sole useful seeded case where two-arm ended at 93 live nodes vs 84 with seeded.
material_findings.C587: Pre-existing width+1 rule would miss the sole v0 positive on the same test as a secondary cross-check; a confirmatory protocol explicitly comparing fixed learned vs width+1 is frozen but incomplete after a hard timeout.

blocker: The 20-seed quartic16 confirmatory matrix exceeded the Python hard execution limit when attempted as one monolithic call. Per runtime rule, no partial printed/in-memory state from that call is evidence.
